linkedin.caption:
Cisco's Node.js and Brotli advisory covers four vulnerabilities, not one identical risk across every device.

CVE-2026-111497: malformed Brotli-compressed input can corrupt decoder memory and may lead to code execution.
CVE-2026-105482: DNS name truncation can make an application resolve a different name from the one it checked.
CVE-2026-105483 and CVE-2026-106069: unusual IP address forms can undermine TLS identity checking under their documented conditions.

Start with the exact model, software release and operating mode. Cisco lists Nexus 3000/9000 standalone NX-OS Guest Shell as impacted; ACI mode and other products have separate status. Under investigation is neither confirmed impact nor an all-clear.

Use Cisco's supported product-specific remediation. Verify availability and compatibility of the Guest Shell 4.9 or NX-OS path for your device; future target dates are not proof that software is downloadable. Do not manually replace bundled Node.js inside an appliance. Back up, define rollback and retain before/after evidence.

The diagram illustrates software behaviour, not a recorded exploit or device test.

Read the detailed QCS assessment:
https://www.qcsstudio.com/security-advisories/cisco-cisco-sa-oct2026-node-js-jj3sq19u

Original Cisco advisory:
https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-oct2026-node-js-Jj3SQ19u
